question.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function and $f(1)=4$. Then the value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \int_4^{f(x)} \frac{2 t}{x-1} d t$, if $f^{\prime}(1)=2$ is

solution.text:
Hint : $\operatorname{Lim}_{x \rightarrow 1} \int_4^{f(x)} \frac{2 t}{x-1} d t,=\operatorname{Lim}_{x \rightarrow 1}\left[\frac{t^2}{x-1}\right]_4^{f(x)}$
$\begin{aligned}
& ==\operatorname{Lim}_{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{[f(x)]^2-4^2}{x-1} \quad\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right)[\because f(1)=4] \\
& =\operatorname{Lim}_{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{2 f(x) f^{\prime}(x)}{1}=2 f(1) f^{\prime}(1)=2(4)(2)=16
\end{aligned}$
